question: The salary decreased by 12%. If the original salary was Rs. 40000, find the new salary.
explanation: Decrease = 12%. So the remaining value is 88% of the original. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%-12\%=88\%\] | Now take 88% of the original salary. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New salary}=40000\times\frac{88}{100}=35200\] | So the new salary is Rs. 35200. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New salary}=35200\]

question: After a 20% decrease, the value became 640. Find the original value.
explanation: After a decrease of 20%, the new value becomes 80% of the original. | \[\Rightarrow 80\%\rightarrow640\] | 80% can also be written as the fraction 4/5. | \[\Rightarrow 80\%=\frac{4}{5}\] | First find the value of 1% by dividing 640 by 80. | \[\Rightarrow 1\%=\frac{640}{80}=8\] | Now multiply the value of 1% by 100 to get the original value. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%=8\times100=800\] | So the original value was 800. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Original value}=800\]

So split the original total. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Initial boys}=400\times\frac{40}{100}=160,\ \text{Initial girls}=240\] | Now decrease the numbers of boys and girls by their respective percentages. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New boys}=160\times\frac{80}{100}=128,\ \text{New girls}=240\times\frac{90}{100}=216\] | Use the new total to find the updated percentage of boys. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New boys percent}=\frac{128}{344}\times100=37.2093\%\] | So the new percentage of boys is 37.2093%. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New boys percent}=37.2093\%\]

question: The current salary is Rs. 48000 and it must become Rs. 36000. Find the required percentage decrease.
explanation: First find how much reduction is needed to reach the target. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Needed reduction}=48000-36000=12000\] | Now compare this reduction with the current salary. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Required decrease}=\frac{12000}{48000}\times100=25\%\] | So the required percentage decrease is 25%. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Required decrease}=25\%\]

question: An inventory of 8000 decreases by 12% every month. Find the inventory after 2 months.
explanation: Each decrease of 12% leaves 88% of the inventory. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%-12\%=88\%\] | Since the same decrease happens for 2 periods, use the retained factor 2 times. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Overall factor}=\left(\frac{88}{100}\right)^{2}\] | Now multiply the current inventory by this overall factor. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Final inventory}=8000\times\left(\frac{88}{100}\right)^{2}=6195.2\] | So the inventory after 2 periods is 6195.2. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Final inventory}=6195\]

question: The population decreased by 25%. If the original population was 4000, find the new population.
explanation: Decrease = 25%. So the remaining value is 80% of the original. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%-20\%=80\%\] | 80% can also be written as the fraction 4/5. | \[\Rightarrow 80\%=\frac{4}{5}\] | Now take 80% of the original salary. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New salary}=20000\times\frac{80}{100}=16000\] | So the new salary is Rs. 16000. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New salary}=16000\]

question: A salary of Rs. 60000 decreased by 20%. Find the decrease amount only.
explanation: Only the reduced part is needed here. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Decrease amount}=20\%\text{ of }Rs. 60000\] | 20% can also be written as the fraction 1/5. | \[\Rightarrow 20\%=\frac{1}{5}\] | So find 20% of the original salary. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Decrease amount}=60000\times\frac{20}{100}=12000\] | So the decrease amount is Rs. 12000. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Decrease amount}=12000\]

question: After a 25% decrease, the value became 450. Find the original value.
explanation: After a decrease of 25%, the new value becomes 75% of the original. | \[\Rightarrow 75\%\rightarrow450\] | 75% can also be written as the fraction 3/4. | \[\Rightarrow 75\%=\frac{3}{4}\] | First find the value of 1% by dividing 450 by 75. | \[\Rightarrow 1\%=\frac{450}{75}=6\] | Now multiply the value of 1% by 100 to get the original value. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%=6\times100=600\] | So the original value was 600. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Original value}=600\]

question: Find the decrease multiplier for a 15% decrease in the salary.
explanation: A decrease of 15% leaves 85% of the original. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%-15\%=85\%\] | Write this remaining percentage as a multiplier. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Multiplier}=\frac{85}{100}=0.85\] | So the decrease multiplier is 0.85. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Multiplier}=0.85\]

question: A salary of Rs. 30000 first decreased by 10% and then by 10%. Find the final salary.
explanation: After the first decrease of 10%, the salary becomes 90% of its original value. | \[\Rightarrow \text{After first decrease}=30000\times\frac{90}{100}=27000\] | Now decrease this new value by 10%. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Final value}=27000\times\frac{90}{100}=24300\] | So the salary after both decreases is Rs. 24300. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Final salary}=24300\]

question: A price decreased first by 15% and then by 15%. Find the overall percentage decrease.
explanation: Convert both decreases into retained factors. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Combined factor}=\frac{85}{100}\times\frac{85}{100}\] | This combined factor shows what fraction of the original still remains. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Combined factor}=\frac{85}{100}\times\frac{85}{100}=0.7225\] | So subtract the remaining fraction from 1 and convert it into percent. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Net decrease}=27.75\%\] | So the overall percentage decrease is 27.75%. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Net decrease}=27.75\%\]

question: salary A was Rs. 40000 and decreased by 12%. salary B was Rs. 45000 and decreased by 10%. Find the difference between their new values.

question: In a group of 200 students, 50% were boys and the rest were girls. If the number of boys decreased by 10% and the number of girls decreased by 15%, find the new percentage of boys.
explanation: At first, 50% of the students are boys. So split the original total. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Initial boys}=200\times\frac{50}{100}=100,\ \text{Initial girls}=100\] | Now decrease the numbers of boys and girls by their respective percentages. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New boys}=100\times\frac{90}{100}=90,\ \text{New girls}=100\times\frac{85}{100}=85\] | Use the new total to find the updated percentage of boys. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New boys percent}=\frac{90}{175}\times100=51.4286\%\] | So the new percentage of boys is 51.4286%. | \[\Rightarrow \text{New boys percent}=51.4286\%\]

question: The current salary is Rs. 40000 and it must become Rs. 30000. Find the required percentage decrease.
explanation: First find how much reduction is needed to reach the target. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Needed reduction}=40000-30000=10000\] | Now compare this reduction with the current salary. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Required decrease}=\frac{10000}{40000}\times100=25\%\] | So the required percentage decrease is 25%. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Required decrease}=25\%\]

question: An inventory of 2000 decreases by 20% every month. Find the inventory after 2 months.
explanation: Each decrease of 20% leaves 80% of the inventory. | \[\Rightarrow 100\%-20\%=80\%\] | 80% can also be written as the fraction 4/5. | \[\Rightarrow 80\%=\frac{4}{5}\] | Since the same decrease happens for 2 periods, use the retained factor 2 times. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Overall factor}=\left(\frac{80}{100}\right)^{2}\] | Now multiply the current inventory by this overall factor. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Final inventory}=2000\times\left(\frac{80}{100}\right)^{2}=1280\] | So the inventory after 2 periods is 1280. | \[\Rightarrow \text{Final inventory}=1280\]
